tasks.title: Add the work phase to the fence judge and to vloop fence check
tasks.goal: W1's core. The judge behind `vloop fence check` and the Copilot hook knows only the review phases, so a Copilot work session cannot be fenced. This task gives it a `work` phase that enforces `fence/work.json` — the same rule set Claude's work sessions run under — plus the adapter's work deny-list stems (the review stems without `rm:*`), and lets work sessions write anywhere in the repository except where S-4 forbids. T2 puts it behind the hook; the review phases must not change by a byte.

references.why: the judge that gains the work phase: its splitting, unwrapping, outright denials and fence matching stay shared with review; only the rule set, the stems, the write rule and the messages differ
the work fence whose Bash(…) deny rules the work phase enforces, read from the embedded file as review reads fence/review.json — never a hand-copied list
the deny list whose stems the judge also enforces; the work phase's stems are the review list without shell(rm:*)
S-4: where a work session may write — not under .git/ or .vloop/ outside .vloop/tmp/ — the rule the work phase's write check enforces

acceptance:
`vloop fence check --phase work --root --tool [--path

] [""]` gives every decision of the brief's two worked-example tables and its apply_patch lines; where the brief shows a message, the deny line is `deny: ` followed by that message without its `vloop fence: ` prefix (the prefix is the hook's, as for review).

Shell in work: the same splitting, unwrapping and outright denials as review (backtick, `$(`, `<(`, `>(`, `eval`, `source`, `.`, unterminated quote, non-literal `-c` string, command word starting with `$`, the shell keywords, subshells); a simple command is denied by a `Bash(…)` deny rule of the embedded `fence/work.json` (`<command> is denied by the work fence (Bash(<rule>))`) or a work deny-list stem (`<command> is denied by the Copilot deny list (<stem>)`). The rules and stems are read from the embedded fence and the adapter's list; a second hand-copied rule list is a violation.

Writes in work (`create`, `edit`, `apply_patch`, a redirection) resolve against --root as in review and are allowed anywhere under the root except under `.git/` or under `.vloop/` outside `.vloop/tmp/` (`write to <path> is not allowed in a work session: nothing under .git/ or .vloop/ but .vloop/tmp/`) and outside the root (`write to <path> is not allowed in a work session: it is outside the repository`); `/dev/null` is allowed.

Reads in work as in review; `skill` only for one of the embedded plugin's skills, else `skill <name> is not vloop's — use /vloop:work`; every other tool, `web_fetch`, `task` and names ending in `_subagent`: `tool <name> is not allowed in a work session`.

`rm` of a file is allowed in work; `rm -rf`, `rm -r`, `rm -R`, `rm -fr` and the rest of the work fence's recursive rules deny; `pnpm add`, `npm install` and `node x.js` are allowed and `pip install` and `sh script.sh` are denied, as the brief decides.

An unknown phase is a usage error, exit 2, with `unknown phase "

": want review, second-review or work`.

The review and second-review phases decide and word every call exactly as before — `rm src/old.ts` with `--phase review` is still `deny: rm src/old.ts is denied by the Copilot deny list (rm:*)`, exit 1. The existing judge tests that pin `work` as an unknown phase change only to the new behaviour, and the work notes name the contract item (W1).

The work phase's rules are covered by committed Go table tests in `internal/fence` that run on every OS in the `go` check, covering every line of the worked example's two tables and the path rules; a work phase with no committed tests is a violation.
No Claude session's argv, fence file or settings changes, and `fence/work.json` and `fence/review.json` are unchanged.

tasks.title: Run work sessions on Copilot: the hook's work phase, the adapter and agent.work = copilot
tasks.goal: W1's hook half and W2's core. With T1's judge, `vloop fence hook --phase work` can fence a Copilot work session; this task lets the Copilot adapter run `/vloop:work <task>` exactly as it runs a review — same plugin, fresh home, guidelines, JSON Lines parsed into session/v4 — with only two differences: its hooks file runs the hook with `--phase work`, and its argv omits `--deny-tool=shell(rm:*)`. `agent.work` then accepts `copilot`. Everything the driver does around the work session stays as it is: the checks after the session are the boundary (S-2, S-4).

references.why: the adapter: the phases it supports, its deny list (work drops only shell(rm:*)) and the hooks file whose --phase must be work for work sessions
the work kind and the Copilot hook: a Copilot work session is a work session in every respect but its agent, and the driver's guards around it are unchanged
S-2 and S-4, the driver is the boundary and where a session may write; P-6, how the work session's model and effort resolve whatever the agent
the Copilot tool names and preToolUse payload the hook reads, and the work replays a Copilot work session must survive

acceptance:
`vloop fence hook --phase work --root ` answers each payload with T1's work decision, the reason being `vloop fence: ` and T1's message, exit 0; an unknown phase is the deny line with `unknown phase "

": want review, second-review or work` and exit 2; the review and second-review phases answer exactly as before.

`agent.work` accepts `claude` (default) and `copilot`, from the file and from `VLOOP_AGENT_WORK`; `agent.plan`, `agent.gate-review` and `agent.verify` still refuse `copilot` (config set exits 2; a run with their variable set to copilot starts no session).

With `agent.work = copilot`, the work session runs `copilot -p "/vloop:work <task>"` with the model and effort P-6 resolves, the plugin by `--plugin-dir`, a fresh home under `.vloop/tmp/` holding a hooks file that runs `fence hook --phase work` in both command forms, the guidelines as custom instructions, and every review deny-list entry on the argv except `--deny-tool=shell(rm:*)`.
A Copilot work session's JSON Lines become a `session/v4` record with phase `work`, agent `copilot`, the model, credits, estimated cost, `cost_source` and `permission_denials`.

A Copilot review or second-review session's argv and hooks file are unchanged (`shell(rm:*)` on the argv, `--phase review`/`second-review` in the hooks file); a Claude session's argv, fence and settings are unchanged.

Everything around the work session is unchanged whatever the agent: the gate, the checks, the guards (a moved ref halts with exit 9; inputs restored), the proposal read from `.vloop/tmp/`, the review and the one commit.

Committed Go tests cover the adapter's work-phase argv (no `shell(rm:*)`, the rest of the list present), its hooks file's `--phase work`, `Supports(work)`, the hook's work phase and `agent.work` accepting copilot; tests that pinned work as unsupported or `work` as an unknown hook phase change only to the new behaviour, and the work notes name the contract item (W1, W2).

tasks.title: Check agent.work = copilot in the run preflight and doctor
tasks.goal: W2's guard rails. An operator who sets `agent.work = copilot` gets what Copilot review already gives: the experimental warning, a refusal while `model.work` is still the Claude default, and the copilot checks — copilot on PATH and runnable, a GitHub login reaching its sessions, K1's refusal of a project skill named like one of vloop's — in `vloop run` and as `vloop doctor` rows. Without these, a run would hand a Claude alias to Copilot or let a project skill shadow `/vloop:work`.

references.why: the Copilot section's warnings and refusals for agent.review, which agent.work now gets in the same words with the key named
P-6: model.work is the work session's model; its default `sonnet` is a Claude alias that Copilot cannot take

acceptance: `vloop run` with `agent.work = copilot` prints `  ! agent.work is copilot: experimental (docs/guide/configuration.md)` and goes ahead; `vloop doctor` prints `! agent.work is copilot: experimental (docs/guide/configuration.md)` and the copilot and copilot login rows.

`vloop run` with `agent.work = copilot` (from the file or `VLOOP_AGENT_WORK`) and `model.work` at its default refuses before any session, exit 1: `vloop: agent.work is copilot but model.work is the default "sonnet", a Claude alias: set model.work to a Copilot model id`.

With `agent.work = copilot`, a project skill directory under `.claude/skills/` or `.github/skills/` named like one of vloop's skills stops `vloop run` with K1's message (`vloop: .claude/skills/work has the name of vloop's work skill; a copilot session may load it instead — rename it`), exit 1, no session, and is an error row in doctor.

With `agent.work = copilot`, no GitHub login reaching the sessions refuses the run naming `agent.work` (`vloop: agent.work is copilot but no GitHub login reaches its sessions: …`), exit 1, and is doctor's copilot login error row; copilot missing or `copilot --version` failing is doctor's copilot error row and stops the run.
With `agent.work = claude`, none of this appears and a project skill named `work` stops nothing; the checks for agent.review and agent.second-review keep their words and behaviour.
Committed tests cover the warning, the model.work refusal, K1 and the login refusal for agent.work (extending the existing doctor and run preflight tests).

tasks.title: Document Copilot work sessions in the fence audit, the configuration guide and the domain pages
tasks.goal: A1's prose. The fence audit, the guide and the domain pages say what a Copilot work session may do and who enforces each rule: the operator reads these to decide whether to trust `agent.work = copilot`, so every sentence must match what T1–T3 built. Prose task: if it fails review twice on wording, it is blocked and the operator finishes it.

references.why: the audit that gains the work fence, classified as the review fence already is: driver after the session, the hook, or neither with what covers it
every deny rule the audit's work part must classify, rule by rule
the agent keys table and the Copilot section that must cover work sessions, the hook's work phase and the experimental label

the session page that today says copilot runs review sessions only and that the hook serves review; it must say copilot runs work, review and second-review sessions and the hook serves the work phase with the work fence
the glossary's hook entry, which must cover the work phase and the work fence
the hook's fail-open limits (B22.2, B22.3) the audit and the guide must state honestly for work sessions too

acceptance: `docs/design-notes/fence-audit.md` gains a part for the work fence, under a heading naming it, that classifies every deny rule of `fence/work.json` and every work deny-list pattern (the review list without `shell(rm:*)`) by who enforces it in a Copilot work session — the driver after the session, the hook, or neither — and says, for each `neither`, what covers it; it says `rm` of a file is allowed and why.

`docs/guide/configuration.md`: the `agent.work` row offers `claude` and `copilot` (experimental); `agent.plan`, `agent.gate-review` and `agent.verify` still offer `claude` alone; the Copilot section covers work sessions — the hook judges them against the work fence, what it allows them, that shell syntax it cannot judge (`if`, `for`, `while`, `$(…)`, subshells) is denied, the model.work refusal and the experimental warning.

`docs/domain/execution/session.md` and the glossary of `docs/domain/domain-model.md` say copilot runs work, review and second-review sessions and the hook serves the work phase with the work fence; nothing still says copilot runs review sessions only.
Every sentence about behaviour matches what T1–T3 built (messages quoted as the code prints them); the `go` check still passes.

tasks.title: Extend the Copilot acceptance kit with a work run on the real CLI
tasks.goal: A1's operator tool. Gates use a stub copilot; only a run on the real CLI proves a Copilot work session works. This task gives the operator a script that runs the fixture brief with `agent.work = copilot` and a given model, plan and review on Claude, and summarises each work session and each task's outcome, so the acceptance at close can be recorded. No gate or check runs it.

references.why: the kit this extends: how its scripts are run, where they write, and that the outcome is recorded in docs/design-notes/copilot-cli-experiments.md
where the operator records the work run's summary, and the session/v4 fields (credits, estimated cost, permission_denials) the summary must report

acceptance: `tools/copilot-acceptance/` gains a script that runs `greet.loop-brief.md` in a scratch repository with a vloop built from this tree, `agent.work = copilot` and `model.work` the model given, plan and review on Claude, and writes a summary listing each work session record (agent, model, credits, estimated cost, `session/v4` validity, its `permission_denials`) and each task's outcome.

The README gains its section: how to run it, what it needs (copilot, a logged-in gh, claude), what it spends, what the summary holds, and that the outcome is recorded in `docs/design-notes/copilot-cli-experiments.md` before close.

The kit's scripts pass `sh -n` and its Python parses; flags, keys and messages of existing vloop commands the script uses are taken from running them, not memory; no gate or check runs the kit, copilot, gh or the network.

tasks.title: Close the run: every gate at once, and the worked example line for line
tasks.goal: The brief's close. Every earlier gate re-runs on the final tree, and the review holds the brief's worked example against the built binary line for line, so nothing a later task changed has broken an earlier one's contract. It builds nothing new unless a gate or a worked-example line fails, and then fixes only that.
acceptance: Every gate T1–T5 passes on the final tree.

Every line of the brief's worked example holds against the built binary: the two `fence check --phase work` tables and the apply_patch lines, the review phase's `rm` line, the unknown phase, the stub run's warning, record, argv and hooks file, and each planted failure.
The `go` check passes on the final tree.
